messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPEN · P1 · model-quality-regression detected for model `redwood-alpha-7b` in eu-west1.
incident-bot: Symptoms: spike in generation re-rolls, increased hallucination reports from support, elevated prompt-level quality regression on benchmark suite. Affected API: `POST /v1/generate`. Runbook: <https://runbooks.internal/redwood/model-quality>. Incident ID: INC-2034501123 :rotating_light:

mike_oncall: ack. I’m on it. spinning up logs and current canary status.

emily_prodeng: I see the canary rolled ~20m ago (deploy id `deploy-2024-11-02-7b`). Any immediate customer errors besides odd outputs?

alesha_support: support -> escalations: two paying customers reported sustained hallucinations & corrupted structured outputs around 10:41 UTC. Customer A saw personal data hallucination, Customer B had truncated JSON. Tickets linked.

beth_research: ran quick eval against our regression set — QA accuracy dropped from ~92% -> 67% on the 10k prompt set in eu-west. Not a latency/cpu issue, this looks model-behavioral.

raj_sre: infra quick-check: no rack-wide cpu/gpu OOMs, but there are ~0.8% 503 spikes correlating with canary. Logs snippet:
```
2024-11-02T10:38:14Z redwood-alpha-7b canary worker id=cl-11 generation_error=none rerolls=3
2024-11-02T10:39:02Z redwood-alpha-7b canary worker id=cl-11 output_valid=false schema_validation=failed
2024-11-02T10:40:59Z redwood-alpha-7b canary worker id=cl-12 rerolls=5
```

mike_oncall: initial mitigation plan: 1) revert canary to previous model revision, 2) pin traffic to stable model variant, 3) notify customers + update status page. Starting step 1 now.

emily_prodeng: prepping rollback PR and model-pin config. Proposed model pin: `model: redwood-alpha-7b
variant: redwood-alpha-7b@rev-2024-10-19-stable`

mike_oncall: rollback command I’m running: 
```
# rollback to previous model revision
redwoodctl deploy rollback --model redwood-alpha-7b --to-revision rev-2024-10-19-stable --region eu-west1
kubectl rollout status deployment/redwood-alpha-7b-canary -n inference
```

incident-bot: UPDATE · rollback initiated by mike_oncall at 2034501205. Automated tests queued.

paul_pm: Draft status page blurb (short):
"We detected a generation quality regression affecting text outputs from the redwood-alpha-7b model in EU-West. We are rolling back to a previous model revision and monitoring. If you rely on structured output, you may see anomalous results; we’ll post updates here."

paul_pm: Draft customer notification (concise):
"Hi — we observed degraded output quality for generation requests served from EU-West using redwood-alpha-7b. We have rolled back to a known-good model revision and are monitoring. No action required on your side; contact support if you continue to see issues. — Redwood Inference"

alesha_support: +1 to concise. For affected customers I recommend the detailed template with list of observed behaviors, ETA for follow-up, and contact routing.

mike_oncall: rollback completed on canary, starting gradual rollout of pinned stable variant to 100% for eu-west. Monitoring metrics now.

raj_sre: metric snapshot (post-rollback, ~6m): gen_quality_index: baseline=0.98 -> canary-during-incident=0.72 -> post-rollback=0.96. 503s back to normal.

beth_research: re-running eval subset, quick-check shows QA accuracy climbed back to 90% in eu-west sample (within noise).

incident-bot: MITIGATION · rollback complete and model-pin applied. Incident status -> "mitigated". Auto-notification queued for subscribers.

mike_oncall: Sending customer notifications now, will post status page update. Alesha, please confirm the support tickets get a personalised note using the detailed template.

alesha_support: On it — drafting two customer messages (short + detailed) and attaching logs and mitigation timeline.

paul_pm: Status page update final copy: 
"Update 10:58 UTC — We rolled back the redwood-alpha-7b model in EU-West to a previous revision after detecting a quality regression. Generation quality is returning to expected levels; customers may temporarily see rate-limited admin requests as we finalize the validation. We’ll post a full incident summary once the postmortem is complete"

mike_oncall: OK. Moving to monitoring phase. Leaving a runbook checklist for the next on-call:
- confirm rollback succeeded across all shards (kubectl rollout status)
- run subset eval (scripts/regression_check.sh --region eu-west1)
- watch customer tickets & add notes
- preserve logs and model artifacts `s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2034501123/`

sara_oncall: @mike_oncall taking handoff at 11:30 UTC. Anything I should be aware of?

mike_oncall: main open items: 1) postmortem owners (emily, raj), 2) support follow-ups for two customers, 3) monitor for recurrence for next 12h. If regression reappears, escalate to oncall-eng-leads and re-pin traffic to fallback cluster in us-central. Runbook link: <https://runbooks.internal/redwood/model-quality#fallback-flow>.

mike_oncall: Handoff notes: mitigation confirmed, metrics stable, customer comms dispatched, postmortem scheduled for tomorrow. Please escalate if QA drops below 85% on the regression suite. :white_check_mark:

sara_oncall: ack and thanks. I’ll keep monitoring dashboards and will notify if anything changes.

emily_prodeng: we’ll own the postmortem. initial suspected root cause: a model variant push included a training-time tokenizer change that subtly altered structured-output conditioning. Investigating exact diff.

raj_sre: saving relevant logs & snapshotting canary artifacts to s3 path. Assigned follow-ups for metric instrumentation improvements to reduce time-to-detect.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED -> mitigated at 2034502234. Postmortem required. Tags: model-quality, rollback, customer-impact.

mike_oncall: closing thread. Thanks team — great coordination.
